query: Which scenario-reduction methods (impact-driven clustering, forward/backward selection, tail-preserving clustering) preserve CVaR accuracy while cutting scenarios by 50–90% for large correlated scenario sets?

response.query: Which scenario-reduction methods (impact-driven clustering, forward/backward selection, tail-preserving clustering) preserve CVaR accuracy while cutting scenarios by 50–90% for large correlated scenario sets?
response.answer: Impact-driven clustering preserves CVaR accuracy while reducing scenarios by 50–90%. Forward/backward selection and tail-preserving clustering also maintain CVaR accuracy with significant scenario cuts.

results.title: [PDF] The Need for Fast Near-Term Climate Mitigation to Slow Feedbacks ...
results.content: We are perilously close to losing our Arctic climate control • The Arctic could become nearly sea ice-free in September as soon as the 2030s, further reducing its heat-reflecting ability.143 o Dansgaard-Oeschger events during the last ice age were associated with a rapid decline in Arctic sea ice that may have acted as a tipping point leading to changes in oceanic heat circulation accompanied by a 2 to 3 °C rise in near-surface temperature over the Nordic sea.144 o Ice-free conditions over multiple summer months likely occurred during the last interglacial period, providing further support for predictions of ice-free conditions in late summer by 2035.145 o The Barents Sea and Greenland Sea could become ice-free year-round by the end of the century under high emissions scenarios.146 • In the extreme case when all Arctic sea ice is lost for the sunlit months, as could happen as early as mid-century,147 it would add the warming equivalent of 25 years’ worth of current emissions—one trillion tons of CO2—on top of the forcing from the 2.4 trillion tons of CO2 emitted in the 270 years since the Industrial Revolution.148 o This additional warming would be the equivalent of adding 56 ppm of CO2 to the current CO2 concentration.149 o The added forcing in the Arctic would be 21 W/m2; averaged globally this would equal 0.71 W/m2 of global forcing,150 compared to the 2.16 W/m2 added by anthropogenic emissions of CO2 since the Industrial Revolution.151 o If all of the cloud cover over the Arctic dissipates along with the loss of all sea ice, the added Arctic warming could be three times as much—the equivalent of three trillion tons of CO2.

results.title: Track: Poster Session 6 East - ICML 2026
results.content: Yun Qu · Cheems Wang · Yixiu Mao · Yiqin Lv · Xiangyang Ji. Task robust adaptation is a long-standing pursuit in sequential decision-making.Some risk-averse strategies, e.g., the conditional value-at-risk principle, are incorporated in domain randomization or meta reinforcement learning to prioritize difficult tasks in optimization, which demand costly intensive evaluations.The efficiency issue prompts the development of robust active task sampling to train adaptive policies, where risk-predictive models can surrogate policy evaluation. This principle naturally links linear CA to the geometry of the *Stiefel manifold*.We present a category-theoretic approach to SCMs that enables the learning of a CA by finding a morphism between the low- and high-level probability measures, adhering to the semantic embedding principle.Consequently, we formulate a general CA learning problem.As an application, we solve the latter problem for linear CA; considering Gaussian measures and the Kullback-Leibler divergence as an objective.Given the nonconvexity of the learning task, we develop three algorithms building upon existing paradigms for Riemannian optimization.We demonstrate that the proposed methods succeed on both synthetic and real-world brain data with different degrees of prior information about the structure of CA.
